extracted.intended_audience: student and working newspaper reporters covering labor disputes and strikes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journalists on how to report strikes, lockouts, and other labor troubles: what to include, how to balance material, and how to use human-interest elements without sacrificing accuracy. Emphasizes factual completeness, presentation of both sides, and context for public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness of labor troubles
rubrics_metrics.description: Strikes, lock-outs, and similar labor troubles, as disturbances in the economic life of the community, are of interest to many readers who are not directly affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important issues of wide-spread interest — such as the recognition of trades unions, the eight-hour day, and a living wage — are often involved in labor disputes. Treat acts of violence committed in connection with strikes as having for the average reader the same kind of interest as other similar acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and accurate presentation of both sides
rubrics_metrics.description: A fair and accurate presentation of the points of view of both the employers and the employees is essential in all stories of this kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements from both sides are important; include formal statements and official positions from employers and union leaders to ensure balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct accounts of living and working conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of living and working conditions, as obtained from workmen and their families often give a better picture of the circumstances that produced the strike than do formal statements by labor leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview workers and families for concrete, on-the-ground details; these human-scale accounts can illuminate causes and consequences more vividly than abstract declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of human-interest and sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Although stories in this class are largely informative, there is also a chance for human interest treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sympathy may be legitimately created for the strikers and their families, especially when they are in actual want or are plainly the victims of oppression. Use human-interest material to illuminate conditions without substituting sentiment for facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide all facts necessary for intelligent public understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the settlement of labor troubles not infrequently is brought about by the influence of public opinion, constructive journalism recognizes the importance of furnishing readers with all of the facts necessary for an intelligent understanding of the issues and conditions involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply contextual background, economic and legal implications, timelines, likely impacts, and any information that helps readers form an informed view; be mindful that reportage can affect outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete specifics in strike reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report detailed factual information such as numbers of employees involved, scope (miles/systems/precincts affected), particulars of demands, percentages and wage figures, and negotiations' status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text show inclusion of exact counts, points in dispute (e.g., wage percentage differences, seniority/promotion rights), names and titles of union and management representatives, and likely effects (number of other employees who would be thrown out, impact on public services). Use such specifics to ground the story.
